notes.whyTheseNumbersChanged: v1's five numbers were round aspirations (250 KB / 416 KB / 300 KB / 1150 KB) written as a gate and never run: no CI job executed check-bundle.mjs, and measured against HEAD on 2026-08-23 THREE of the five failed — entry 287,644 > 256,000, initial 482,196 > 425,984, total 1,273,275 > 1,177,600. A budget nobody ran is not a budget. v2 replaces the wishes with a RATCHET: each ceiling is the measured value of a green build plus a stated margin, so a regression is caught on the day it lands instead of being invisible behind a number that was already red. The aspiration is not thrown away — it is kept below, as `target`, which is where it belonged all along.
notes.margin: ~5% over measured, on every byte ceiling. Wide enough that ordinary feature work does not churn this file; far tighter than the 76,736-byte regression that returning the dev MockCore to the entry chunk would cause, which the v1 ceilings would have accepted in silence.

notes.whyTheseNumbersChangedAgain: 2026-08-26: the entry ceiling was RE-BASELINED 174,000 -> 199,000, and the reason is written down because `notes.margin` says a ceiling raised without knowing which change spent the bytes is not a ceiling. It was red on HEAD before this session touched anything, and BISECTED rather than guessed: eleven commits built from clean detached checkouts, entry chunk measured by `stat` each time — 86df2ea 166,665 / ff5b73a 167,559 / e5f74ff 167,552 / 1ec9478 167,526 / b610775 167,535 / f5b5d19 168,044 / 6932aab 168,044 / 096be3a 168,044 / 4e845c5 168,769 / b2cd35e 168,769 / 58e181c 188,679. One commit, +19,910 bytes, straight through a 174,000 ceiling. `58e181c` landed `theme/icons.tsx` (878 lines, 161 inline-SVG drawings — 166 path literals costing 7,575 bytes in the entry alone), `theme/assets.tsx` and `theme/timeline.tsx` as NEW files; `icons.tsx` and `assets.tsx` are reachable from first paint because the Engines rail, the header, the hierarchy and the empty state all draw marks before anything else loads. That is `first-paint.json`'s counter-rule exactly: a surface whose job is to be there when you first look cannot be the one that loads last, and an icon that pops in after the chunk arrives is the ADR-131 blank-control defect arriving late instead of never. So the bytes are DELIBERATE and the stale number is the defect. The new ceiling is a measured green build (189,845, this tree, after ADR-147 moved the settings-sheet family out of the entry) plus the same ~5% margin. ADR-147's own contribution is 1,166 bytes of that, measured against 58e181c's 188,679. The INITIAL ceiling moves with it and for the same reason, not as a second judgement: initial = the entry plus the two chunks it statically imports (vendor-react, vendor-state), so every byte of the entry is also an initial byte. HEAD measured 383,231 against 378,000 — red on its own, before this session — and this tree measures 384,397. Both new ceilings are a measured green build plus ~5%. The other three were and remain green at both points: largest 256,274 <= 270,000, total 1,267,741 <= 1,272,000, 33 chunks >= 24.

notes.whyTheseNumbersChangedAgain2026_08_31: 2026-08-31: the ENTRY ceiling moved 199,000 -> 200,000 and the bytes are named first, which is the rule this file already states. Two production `vite build`s from the same tree, one file apart: entry 195,644 -> 199,268 (+3,624), and every other chunk is byte-identical. What spent them: the three selection verbs no gesture can express plus the content-aware one — Select all / none / invert / similar as palette commands, the Ctrl+A chord, `applySelection` and `app/selectSimilar.ts` (the mesh-handle and component-signature match, and the plain-language reason it reports). NOT code-split, and the reason is the same one the marquee bytes carry two notes above: the command LIST is built during App's render so the palette can be handed a complete set the moment it opens, and a verb that arrived after the palette did would be a row that is sometimes there. `similarTo` alone is ~1 KB of the 3,624 and could be split behind a dynamic import; a chunk and a round trip for one kilobyte, on a surface already lazy, is not a trade worth making. A further +1,243 came from moving those four command objects out of `App`'s render into `app/selectionCommands.tsx`, and that byte cost bought a specific thing: the `shots` gate can now photograph the SHIPPED rows (`palette-selection`) instead of a copy of them written out in the scene, which is the class of evidence this repository keeps finding to be worthless. Entry measured **195,644 -> 200,511** end to end. The new ceiling is that build plus ~0.25%, the same tight margin the 2026-08-27 re-baseline used. The TOTAL ceiling moves with it, and not as a second judgement: 1,277,651 -> 1,282,518 is the same bytes counted again, because the entry is part of the total and nothing else moved. 1,281,000 -> 1,285,000, the measured build plus ~0.3%. Initial (393,955 <= 403,000), largest and chunk count did not move and are green. THE 2026-08-27 MERGE NOTE STILL STANDS AND NOW HAS A FOURTH LANE: ADR-154 (+10,385), ADR-155 (+3,253) and this (+3,624) have each re-baselined for their own measured bytes against a base that does not include the others. Whoever merges last must RE-MEASURE from the merged tree rather than adding these numbers together.
notes.whyTheseNumbersChangedAgain2026_08_27: 2026-08-27: the TOTAL ceiling moved 1,272,000 -> 1,281,000 and the bytes are named first, which is the rule this file already states. Two production builds from the same base (`15b43fc`, the tip of origin/main) in a detached worktree vs this tree: total 1,271,852 -> 1,277,561 (+5,709), and the diff is ONE chunk — the entry, 189,845 -> 195,554. Every other chunk is byte-identical. What spent them: box selection on the stage (`app/marquee.ts`, `app/StageMarquee.tsx`), the modifier-carrying pick and the drag lifecycle in `App.tsx`, `store/selectionText.ts`, and four new client methods in `transport/session.ts` (plus the MockCore selection they need to be honest in the dev build). NONE of it is code-split, deliberately: a rectangle you drag is drawn DURING the gesture, so a lazy chunk would arrive after the drag it is meant to draw — `first-paint.json`'s counter-rule, the same argument the icon set makes. The new ceiling is this measured build plus ~0.27%, the same tight margin 1,272,000 carried over its own 1,267,741. The entry (195,554 <= 199,000) and initial (381,106 <= 403,000) ceilings are UNCHANGED and green; largest and chunk count did not move. MERGE NOTE, because it will bite whoever lands last: two concurrent lanes have separately measured +10,385 (ADR-154, scene cameras) and +3,253 (ADR-155, the vector row) against this same base, and each has re-baselined this number for its own bytes alone. The sum does not fit under any of the three ceilings. The last merge must RE-MEASURE and re-baseline from the merged tree; raising a ceiling now to pre-approve bytes nobody in this lane has measured would be the exact defect `notes.margin` is written against.
